2_Introduction: With the improved uniformity of SAM, the SAM-based devices showed a maximum PCE of 25.7614%, with a VOC of 1.1862 V, FF of 84.8668%, and JSC of 25.59 mA/cm². The perovskite composition is Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0, and the initial stock perovskite solution is 1.65 mol/L. Then, the prepared precursor solution was spin-coated onto the ITO substrate at 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s. During the second step, antisolvent CB (150 µL) was dropped at the middle of the spinning substrate 15 s prior to the end of the spinning. The substrates were immediately transferred to the hotplate and annealed at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The triple-cation Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3 perovskite, engineered with a high-concentration 1.65 M precursor, undergoes rapid crystallization driven by a two-step spin-coating process (1000 rpm for 5 s, 5500 rpm for 30 s) and the precise introduction of 150 µL chlorobenzene antisolvent 15 seconds before spinning completion; this protocol promotes dense, rapid nucleation, while subsequent annealing at 110°C for 15 minutes facilitates grain growth and reduces bulk defects, with the mixed A-site cations synergistically stabilizing the perovskite α-phase and suppressing halide ion migration. The concurrent application of a uniform self-assembled monolayer (SAM) on the ITO substrate critically modulates the interface, where its improved coverage and molecular ordering provide effective surface passivation, suppress non-radiative recombination at the buried contact, and optimize energy-level alignment for enhanced hole extraction. The synergy between the controlled perovskite crystallization, which yields a morphologically uniform film with reduced defect density, and the homogenous SAM interface, which minimizes interfacial losses, collectively establishes superior charge transport pathways and markedly lowers recombination, ultimately yielding a champion device with a VOC of 1.1862 V, a JSC of 25.59 mA/cm², an FF of 84.8668%, and a PCE of 25.7614%.
